findings.how: New pure app/renderer/overlay/layout.ts with pillSpot() and pillBottom(). placeStatus() in the overlay renderer runs on state, init and resize. When the padded ring of the control Ember works on is under the pill at the top (40 px, centred), the pill moves to the bottom-centre, 20 px above the work area (.status.low). OverlayInit now carries the display's workArea (overlay.ts initFor). .focus has z-index 4, so the ring is drawn above the pill. c29f5f6 does the layout read only when the status, the control or the screen changed. Checked in the built overlay on the reviewer's address bar (260,48 920x32 at 1440x900): the pill moves to y=784. For a control mid-screen, or no control, it stays at y=40.
findings.test: test/unit/overlay-pill.test.ts: 6 tests (pillSpot top/bottom/ribbon/tall control, pillBottom, init carries workArea). All failed before and pass now.

findings.how: Round 1: besideControl() in follow.ts takes `avoid`. When its usual spot is under the handle or the cards, it tries the other side, then above, then below. OverlayManager parks Ember with that display's keep-off area, and re-parks it when cards that come up cover its spot. layout.ts cardsCorner() moves the card stack to the bottom-left while the control's ring is under it at the bottom-right. .focus (z-index 4) is drawn above .tasks (3). Round 2, the verifier's band: keepOff(display) now returns Rect[]. The handle and cards make one area only when they overlap across (cards stacked above the handle). Otherwise each is its own area, so cards at the bottom-left no longer make a band across the bottom. followTarget() lifts Ember above whichever area it covers (and above the next, if that lift lands on one). besideControl() takes a spot only when it covers none. Both still accept a single Rect, so existing callers and tests are unchanged. setCards re-parks when any area covers the spot. The verifier's own scratch test (relfix-verify/overlay/zz-verify-band.test.ts) now logs keepOff=[{1154,660,200x56},{16,555,270x101}], and the hold-still spot is (730,660.74) with the cards on either side. Before, it was y=515 with the cards on the left. Output saved in relfix-verify/overlay/band-after.txt. Its first case now fails by design, because it asserted the band.
findings.test: test/unit/overlay-keepoff.test.ts, describe 'the handle at the bottom-right and the cards moved to the bottom-left'. 3 new tests failed before: the hold-still spot was 145.74 px off the no-cards spot; followTarget over the handle was not lifted; besideControl beside the handle parked under it. All pass now. Round 1's tests ('Ember beside a control near the task cards', 'the task cards and the ring round a control') still pass.

findings.how: OverlayManager.keepOff(display) covers only the handle (if it is on that display) and that display's own cards, clipped to its work area. It is no longer one union over every display. The follow tick and setState's hold-still spot pass the cursor's display. The park beside a control passes the control's display. Round 2 also returns areas that don't touch as separate rects (see #126).
findings.test: test/unit/overlay-keepoff.test.ts 'what Ember keeps off, with more than one display' simulates OverlayManager.tick() on two 1920x1080 displays. Before the fix, Ember settled 231 px off the cursor with the second display on the left and 517 px off with stacked displays. findings.how: Each frame from main carries `on`, the id of the display nearest Ember's centre (it is part of the still-frame check too). findings.test: test/unit/overlay-keepoff.test.ts 'Ember near the seam between two displays': 3 tests. They failed before (on undefined, no bubbleHere) and pass now.

verifierProblems.what: busyLine now wins over every idle word, not only over "Ready". In the built handle (relfix-verify/overlay/h/handle.mjs), base vs fix with one running task: idle "Waiting for tasks" gave "Waiting for tasks" on base and gives "Working on 1 task…" on fix. "Reconnecting…" and "Copilot problem" behave the same way, both in the pill and in the fallback card. This matters because host.ts:960-966 sets phase error/not-answering with waitingForTasks exactly while tasks are at work. So idleWord's "Waiting for tasks" can now never show. That word is the only one that tells the user why Ember isn't answering them and that it will reconnect once the tasks are done. The finding asked for the count only "when nothing else is to be said".
verifierProblems.fix: Let the task count replace only "Ready" (or a missing idle word). Add a pure helper in app/renderer/overlay/stack.ts: `idleLine(idle: string | undefined, tasks) => idle && idle !== "Ready" ? idle : busyLine(tasks) ?? idle ?? null`. In handle/main.ts use `s.status ?? (said || idleLine(s.idle, s.tasks) || "Ready")` for the pill and `s.status ?? idleLine(s.idle, s.tasks)` for the fallback card. Add unit tests: "Waiting for tasks" and "Reconnecting…" stay as they are with tasks running; "Ready" becomes "Working on 1 task…".

verifierProblems.what: OverlayManager.keepOff(display) still merges the handle and the cards into one box. Once the renderer moves the cards to the bottom-left (new in this branch), the handle (bottom-right) and the cards no longer touch, so the box becomes a band across the whole bottom of the display. My scratch test (relfix-verify/overlay/zz-verify-band.test.ts, run against 878b8c5) shows this. On a 1366x768 display with the cards at the bottom-left, keepOff = {x:16,y:555,width:1338,height:161}. Then I set focus on Next at (1210,620) and cleared it with a done answer, cursor at (683,690). Ember's hold-still spot is y=660.7 with the cards on the right but y=515 with the cards on the left: 146 px above the cursor, nowhere near the cards or the handle. This happens every time in that sequence. setState(focus:null) parks Ember before the renderer has moved the cards back, and setCards re-parks only while focus is set, so Ember stays there while the answer is up. It is the same kind of union-band bug that #127 fixed.
verifierProblems.fix: Stop merging boxes that don't touch. Have keepOff return Rect[]: the handle and the cards separately, or one merged box only when they overlap horizontally (cards stacked above the handle). Make followTarget and besideControl in follow.ts take `readonly Rect[]`: followTarget lifts Ember above the rect it overlaps; besideControl treats a spot as clear only when it overlaps none. Add a test with the cards at the bottom-left, the handle at the bottom-right and the cursor at the bottom-centre: the hold-still spot after focus clears must equal the spot with no cards.

verifierProblems.what: #130 is implemented twice. fix/bubble commit 8b66ef8 (#19) makes the same change with different copy: screen-reader word "Queued: " in overlay STATE_WORD and handle TASK_WORD, against this branch's "Waiting its turn: ". fix/bubble edits the STATE_WORD line in app/renderer/overlay/main.ts, which this branch moved into stack.ts. Both branches add --sym-queued (slightly different clock path) and the [data-status="queued"] rule, and both change the tasks.ts mapping and the TaskCard type. A careless merge leaves two names for one state (copy rule: the same name for the same thing everywhere) and conflicts in six files.
